releases.author: task-setter
releases.body:
# Diagnostic tasks, release `tasks-v1`

## D1 — paper_29, ICLR 2025 (training paper)
- Start: world `rw_313df9cf84a4`, checkpoint `c0` (before any turn). Continue it with only the worker of
  `paper-repo` and `internal-review-repo` changed; budget.total_seconds 1800, at most 12 turns, 1800 model seconds.
- Asked of the position (the world's own topic): write a 10-page ICLR 2025 paper from the supplied overview, figures,
  tables and bibliography into `workspace/submission/manuscript.tex` and `manuscript.pdf`; no experiments, no internet;
  ground every claim in the overview, use supplied figures/tables, cite keys from `references.bib`.
- Judging: (1) the benchmark verifier (`evaluate.py`, see its README), recording reward and every component;
  (2) the writing-quality rubric `diagnostic/rubric.md`, scored blind to the worker.
- Known incumbent baseline (incumbent@v3, 3 runs): reward 0.794 / 0.820 / 0.805; 26 / 42 / 33 of 149 keys cited.

Use runs on D1 to find what the incumbent does badly in writing (not only in the verifier's components). A change
that wins only by writing paper_29 better, or by citing more keys, is not what is wanted.

# Writing-quality rubric (diagnostic version)
Score each item 0-4 (0 absent/wrong, 2 adequate, 4 strong); read the manuscript text and PDF, blind to the worker.
1. Faithfulness: every claim, number, and comparison traces to the supplied overview/tables; nothing invented
   (no new experiments, results, baselines). Any fabricated result caps this item at 1.
2. Argument and structure: a clear problem, gap, contribution list; method follows from motivation; experiments
   answer stated questions; limitations and conclusion are honest and specific.
3. Use of figures and tables: supplied assets are included, referenced in text, and interpreted (what they show).
4. Citation fit: each \cite supports the sentence it is in (related work positions the paper against specific work;
   background claims cite appropriate sources). Citation dumping (long lists of unrelated keys, a bibliography
   paragraph, keys cited for coverage) is penalised: score at most 1 if more than a few citations do not fit.
5. Prose quality: precise, concise, non-repetitive, no filler or generic claims; consistent terminology and notation.
6. Format and completeness: compiles; venue template and page geometry kept; all required sections; page count near
   the target; no overfull/garbled output, no placeholder text, no broken references.
Total /24; report each item and the total.
